$comment: SEAM MANIFEST — which user-facing seams have a test that ENTERS the seam, not just the inner unit. A seam is COVERED only when the spec (a) exists, (b) contains seamEvent — the gesture/call proving it enters, and (c) contains negativeSpec — the no-op/refusal assertion. Statuses: COVERED (all three verified) · COVERED_NO_NEGATIVE (enters the seam, negative case MISSING — an honest admission) · OPEN (no seam-entering spec). The gate fails only on a FALSE claim, never on an honest admission. Evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-15-seam-coverage/SEAM-COVERAGE.md

seams.note: Replaces the source-text guard: IntentPanel is driven end-to-end with a REAL store (the bridge refuses equal before/after hashes, so a mock store can never register) and the REAL ledger plus a witness ledger both see the row. Kill switch off → register is never called while the route still runs. The privacy boundary is asserted at the call site too.
seams.negativeSpec: NEGATIVE: with the ledger off the same gesture never reaches register
drift guard
seams.note: Compares the shipped manifest against the live grammar + hashes. This is the b7c1919c class of check, done right.

The failure this seam guards is a 404: the spec extracts the loader's MANIFEST_PATH from source, resolves it under public/ and asserts the file exists AND is the very manifest the artifact lock validated; model.url and features.url are asserted too (fetched unconditionally), while runtime.module is asserted only when a non-onnx kind would actually fetch it — under the shipped onnx kind it is latent metadata. A missing path fails with 'which is not on disk'.
seams.negativeSpec: which is not on disk
refuses
seams.note: 550 call sites across 37-41 spec files; the destructive-gate refusal specs are the negative case.

Every ctx in the old suite was a hand-rolled fake, so dispatch → REAL store → undo depth was never asserted. Now kyx_tracks setGain writes the real document, pushes exactly one history entry, and ctx.undo() restores it; kyx_state and listPresets leave both document and undo stack untouched.
seams.negativeSpec: NEGATIVE: a read tool leaves the document AND the undo stack untouched
no ghost sample
seams.note: Driven through the real REC / STOP buttons, not the inner helper: a failed durable save must roll the already-playable resample back out of the bank (no ghost sample), offer no take and return the panel to idle. Verified by mutation — disabling the rollback in src/sample-library/bank-persist.ts turns exactly this spec red.

seams.negativeSpec: does not start a session for checkpoint save/list/diff
seams.note: Wave 1/A: the pre-session checkpoint is taken on the FIRST document-mutating call of a session only. Entered through the real headless MCP host (the same wrapper every transport uses); the negative specs pin that reads, runtime tools, dry-runs and checkpoint save/list/diff never start a session.

seams.negativeSpec: keeps the revert disabled while the session checkpoint is not durable
seams.note: Wave 1/A: the revert commits ONE undoable restoreSnapshot command from the panel, and closes the session. The negative spec pins that a non-durable checkpoint offers no revert at all (disabled, with the reason shown) instead of a button that cannot work.

seams.negativeSpec: aborts the owner's signal and settles as cancelled
seams.note: Wave 1/B: cancellation aborts the owner's signal and settles the job exactly once — the negative assertions pin that a cancelled job cannot be cancelled twice, cannot be revived by a late done(), and that the watchdog fails a lost owner instead of leaving it running.

seams.negativeSpec: stays quiet when the frozen buffer matches
seams.note: Wave 2/D: the strip is driven through the real component with a remembered signature — a mismatching signature shows the badge and RE-FREEZE, while a matching one AND an unknown one (no signature) both stay quiet, because an unprovable staleness must never be claimed.

seams.negativeSpec: a cancel from the Activity Center settles cleanly
seams.note: Wave 2/C reproduction half: the button drives the real verifyRenderStamp runner (only the offline renderer is mocked, jsdom has no OfflineAudioContext). Match is the ONLY success — a mismatch or an unhashable file settles the Job Center job as FAILED so no completion notice can say ✓ about a file that did not reproduce — and a cancel leaves no verdict and no stuck button.

seams.negativeSpec: not an audition
seams.note: Wave A: entered through the REAL panel (type the brief, press DO IT). The default must yield a multi-candidate auditionable bank with ONE explained winner and NO single-result fallback; the negative spec spies the budget to the lean value and pins the honest constrained-device outcome (USE RESULT, nothing to audition) — proving the budget reaches the request instead of being decoration.

seams.seamEvent: aligns a late phrase onto its entry
seams.negativeSpec: ignores a mismatched shift list
seams.note: Vocal-first loop, the one step that did not exist: a phrase that entered a latency-scale step late gets its leading silence skipped so it lands on the entry it was recorded for — measured from the take's own signal, applied inside the SAME placement command (one undo), and reported ('aligned onto its entry (+40 ms)'). NEGATIVEs are the product rules: a deliberate late entry (outside the bounded search window) is never auto-touched, a low-confidence rise is never acted on, and a shift list that does not line up with the loop passes is ignored rather than guessed at. The measurement is best-effort by construction — a buffer without channel data must never take the placement down with it.

seams.negativeSpec: never turns a MISSING source into a quiet pass
seams.note: One downloadable artifact (markdown + JSON) that answers 'did this app lose my work, and is anything it told me not true?'. The NEGATIVEs are the point: a check that could not run is `unknown` (never a quiet ✓), a report with unavailable checks is `partial` rather than `clean`, and the collector survives both a throwing and a MISSING source — because the report is what you open when something is already wrong. The download path is pinned through the real export flow in tests/ui/ExportPanel.test.tsx.

seams.negativeSpec: refuses with the reason
seams.note: Session tape: the journal is filled by the gestures themselves (DO IT → ⚡, USE → ★, a route action → ✎) and REWIND goes through the store's own history jump, so the branch is redoable and everything after it detaches. The NEGATIVE pins the honest refusal: a step that applied nothing reports why (tests/session-tape.test.ts pins the pruned-window and first-state refusals too) instead of silently landing on a different state.

seams.entryPoint: scripts/fit-rerank-weights.mjs (adjudicateShadow over the audio-fit ledger + human picks)
seams.negativeSpec: refuses to stage an experiment
seams.note: CI for taste: the shipped default weight is the shadow policy, the fitted one the active policy, and the verdict is which ordering would have picked what the human kept — computed from the recorded finalist coordinates, so the counterfactual costs no render. NEGATIVEs pin the honest cases: identical weights are not an experiment, fewer than two human picks is no evidence, and a policy comparison never claims a musical quality it cannot measure.

seams.entryPoint: src/intent/reaction-rerank-feedback.ts (npm run rerank:fit) + IntentPanel USE registration
seams.seamEvent: the audio-fit ledger records the SAME id the pipeline stamps on the result
seams.negativeSpec: drops the generation when the human reverted the applied candidate
seams.note: F2's last line — reactions feed the rerank-weight fit. The join is proven at the SOURCE (real pipeline + real rerank, only the offline renderer faked): the recorded observation and the stamped result share one generationId, a human undo DROPS the generation instead of training toward a rejected pick, and a human pick RE-TARGETS the kept candidate — a change that moves the FITTED WEIGHT, not just a field (tests/reaction-rerank-feedback.test.ts). The panel spec (tests/ui/reaction-candidate-use.test.tsx) pins that USE actually records it, and the kill switch still silences it.

seams.negativeSpec: returns the input array itself when no ledger is active
seams.note: Wave B / pre-registered bias guard: reactions REORDER already-validated interpretations and nothing else — the specs pin the reorder against a REAL ledger, member/length preservation, the identity return when there is no evidence, and the kill switch.

seams.negativeSpec: stops settling once the caller detaches
seams.note: Wave B: F1's third settle seam, wired where the transport actually exists. Driven against a REAL Transport and a REAL ledger — including NEGATIVEs that matter: the subscription's initial notification settles nothing, a null ledger subscribes to nothing, and a detached handler stops settling.

seams.seamEvent: shows the measured why next to the winning candidate
seams.negativeSpec: stays silent without a rationale
seams.note: Wave E1: the explanation is a pure derivation from measured scores (tests/selection-reasons.test.ts enters the real pipeline and asserts selection.rationale), and this surface spec pins that the note attaches to the WINNER only and disappears entirely when there is nothing measured to say.

seams.negativeSpec: fails the determinism check when the second run picks a different winner
seams.note: Wave E2: the committed score is re-run through the REAL deterministic pipeline (parser → plan → gates → ranker → E1 rationale) and any non-timing drift fails — a moved winner hash, a lost rationale, a flipped check, or the ranker path changing under the benchmark. Re-blessing is deliberate (taste:benchmark:bless) and preserves humanGrades; the baseline's humanGrades stays null because no machine grades taste.

seams.negativeSpec: keeps the file layout valid without an iXML chunk
seams.note: Wave 2/C: the manifest is written into a REAL encoded WAV and read back through the RIFF walker (hostile names/prompts, odd payload pad byte), and a file WITHOUT the chunk still has an exact RIFF size — the no-regression case for every existing exporter. The end-to-end step is pinned too: tests/ui/ExportPanel.test.tsx clicks EXPORT MASTER and parses the manifest out of the blob the panel hands to the save boundary.

seams.negativeSpec: NEGATIVE: the kill switch reaches the panel — the same history reorders nothing
seams.note: The F2 rule (reactions REORDER gated candidates, never create/drop/edit one) is only true of the product if the CHIPS a human clicks are reordered. The ordering function had unit coverage; this drives the real panel with a real seeded ledger: a kept RETURN fader outranks returned SEND asks (opposite of the router order), while no-decisions, pending-only and the kill switch all keep the router order byte-for-byte, with an identical chip set. Verified by mutation — disabling the bias turns exactly the kept-first spec red.
